idiom_name: language-neutral: a 0..1 optional accessor and a 0..n traversal accessor (get-or-default, modify-each) over a structure
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: name the path once, as two operations - a get that returns zero or one value, so absence is a value rather than an exception, and a modify/set that returns the whole structure with only the focused elements changed. For the plural case define one traversal that visits every matching element, reassembles results with the chosen combining policy (first error, all errors, collected list), and specifies what happens when nothing matches: identity no-op by default, or a documented default value. Keep the accessor separate from the update function so the same path serves reading and writing.
code_sketch:
get(path, s)        -> Option[T]   # 0..1: absence is a value
modify(path, f, s)  -> S           # 0..n: every matching target, structure preserved
# zero targets: modify returns s unchanged; get returns empty
# compose: modify(compose(p, q), f, s)
pitfalls: Repeating the path inline instead of naming it: the read and write views drift apart.
Skipping the zero-target rule: callers cannot tell whether nothing matched or something failed.
Assuming exactly one target where the structure may hold many, or none.
Treating an Optional as a total Lens: a missing focus is not a value to unwrap; use getOption or getOrModify, or make absence an explicit domain error.
Assuming a Traversal chooses one match: getAll or modify applies to zero or many foci; use a short-circuiting search when first-match semantics are required.
Adopting optics solely to remove one null check: abstraction and dependency cost can obscure a simple map or optional-chain expression, so keep the direct idiom for a one-off path.
